notes: ANALYST PASS (iteration 1): (1) Only with-skill failure is an eval-authoring bug, not a skill bug: eval-4 asserted 'security_sweep queued' but the run correctly skipped it as redundant when the main lane IS the security review; reword the assertion. (2) NON-DETERMINISM FOUND: the 'fresh window' heuristic is self-declared — 5 of 9 runs called the window fresh and used fanout_cap_fresh=5, eval-1 used cap 3. This neutralizes every cap-3 expectation. Fix: deterministic freshness (only explicit 'throttle fresh' or a host-provided window signal). (3) lint_sweep/tech_debt_notes have no first-class routing keys — eval-5 bounced off fallback_route noise before re-resolving via boilerplate_scaffolding; amplifiers.md should name the exact --task key per extra. (4) Baseline 0% is by construction (no skill = no routing), so the delta measures existence, not quality — the qualitative outputs are the real signal here. (5) Routing overhead in dry-run: ~+17.7k tokens / +114s vs baseline — the cost of the state gate + adapter + resolver calls; acceptable for a router, worth keeping lean. (6) Deterministic core (pins, band audits, one-band fallback, state gate) behaved identically across all 9 runs — variance is confined to the judgment layer (freshness, extras applicability).
